averaging.","A map error leads to getting lost; a theory error in bridge building leads to physical collapse, raising the stakes of the 'convention'."],"overturn_conditions":["If the GPS system itself was shown to rely on inductive generalizations from past traffic data to predict route viability, the analogy would fail to support a non-inductive basis.","If the 'updated map' was chosen because it felt more intuitive rather than because it incorporated recent falsifications of old routes."],"shared_structure":["Preference for the most recently validated map despite no guarantee it covers new terrain.","Rejection of older maps known to contain errors.","Action taken without inductive certainty of the map's total accuracy."],"source_memory_refs":["nav_system_update"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a driver rationally chooses the updated GPS over a known-wrong paper map without believing the GPS is infallible, a scientist rationally chooses the corroborated theory without believing it is probable."]},"claim":"Preferring the better-corroborated theory for action is defensible on Popper's terms not as an inductive inference that the theory is true or probable, but as a non-inductive, critical decision to act on the hypothesis that has withstood the most severe attempts at falsification, thereby minimizing the risk of known error while accepting that future falsification remains possible.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If corroboration is interpreted as assigning a higher logical probability logical asymmetry between verification and falsification. Acting on this theory is a rational convention to avoid acting on theories already known to be flawed, without claiming the chosen theory will succeed.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
